question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=2x$, the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ can be computed using the definition of the derivative. The first few steps of this calculation are shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2(x+h)-2x}{h} \\  & =…\end{aligned}
$$

Finish the calculation, and hence find ${f}^{′}(x).$

current_example.problem: Given $y =x^2,$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}$ using the limit of a difference quotient.
current_example.worked_solution:
We let $y=f(x)$ and apply the formula for the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{(x+h)^{2}-{x}^{2}}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{{x}^{2}+2xh+{h}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2xh+{h}^{2}}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}(\frac{2xh}{h}+\frac{{h}^{2}}{h}) \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}(2x+h) \\  & =2x+0 \\  & =2x\end{aligned}
$$
